title: Week 9 Analysis
subtitle: The Saints jump from last to second, and Cadegn's lead shrinks to 11.
intro_paragraphs: Only two divisions changed order this week, the NFC North and the NFC South, but they moved points for six of the seven bettors. Cadegn lost 11 and is at 65, still in first, but the lead over second is down from 19 to 11. Mike T gained 6, the best week in the pool, and is alone in 2nd at 54. Hume is the only bettor whose score didn't change at all.
Pittsburgh and Tennessee had the only byes this week. Everyone else played, which is why so many teams are now at eight or nine games.

fun_facts.heading: The NFC South Flips Again
fun_facts.body: New Orleans was the only NFC South team to win this week, and that was enough to go from last to second. The Panthers lost and stayed first at 3-5 (ahead of the 3-5 Saints on a tiebreaker), and the Buccaneers and Falcons both lost and are now 3-6. All four teams have losing records and are within one game of each other. The new order is Panthers, Saints, Buccaneers, Falcons. Mike T and Dilger both picked the Saints second and the Falcons last, so each gained 6. Everyone who was scoring there last week lost: Cadegn 8, Dustin 6, and Farmer 3.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn Gives Back 11
fun_facts.body: Last week Cadegn's NFC South was worth 8: the Falcons in third, the Saints in last, and the bottom-2 bonus. The Saints' win wiped all of it out. The Bears moving from second to first in the NFC North cost another 3. Cadegn still has the most perfect divisions (2), the most top-2 bonuses (3), and is tied for the most bottom-2 bonuses (2), plus 4 of 8 division-winner picks currently right, the most in the pool. But the lead is 11, the closest anyone has been since Week 7.

fun_facts.heading: Mike T Moves Up to 2nd
fun_facts.body: Mike T's only change was the NFC South, and it was all good: the Saints in second and the Falcons in last, +6. That put Mike T at 54, alone in 2nd, and with 13 exact hits out of 32, the most in the pool, one more than Cadegn. Mike T was tied for 3rd last week and is now the closest chaser.

fun_facts.heading: Dustin and Dilger Tie on Points
fun_facts.body: Dustin and Dilger are both at 51 and went opposite directions to get there. Dustin lost all 6 NFC South points: Dustin's two hits there were the Buccaneers second and the Falcons third, and the Saints' jump pushed both down a spot. Dilger gained 6 in the NFC South but lost 3 in the NFC North, for +3. Neither has more perfect divisions (one each), so the second tiebreaker decides it: Dustin has two top-2 bonuses to Dilger's one, so Dustin is 3rd and Dilger is 4th.

fun_facts.heading: Tom and Hume: Dead Even
fun_facts.body: Tom and Hume are tied for 5th at 45, and they match on every tiebreaker the pool has: one perfect division, one top-2 bonus, two bottom-2 bonuses, and 10 exact hits each. Without the point-total tiebreaker, they're officially tied. Hume got there by standing still. Nothing in Hume's picks moved this week. Tom lost 3 when the Bears passed Detroit, the same NFC North hit four bettors took.

fun_facts.heading: Nobody Has Anything in the NFC North
fun_facts.body: Chicago won and moved to first at 7-2. Detroit (6-2) passed Minnesota (6-2), which lost, and Green Bay is last at 6-3. That's the only division where every team has at least six wins. Dilger, Tom, Cadegn, and Farmer had all picked the Bears second, and that was the only thing anyone was getting there, so all four lost 3. All seven bettors now have 0 points in the NFC North. All seven picked the Lions to win it, and nobody picked the Bears.

fun_facts.heading: Farmer Drops 18 Back
fun_facts.body: Farmer lost 3 in the NFC North and 3 in the NFC South and is last at 27. The gap to Tom and Hume is 18, the widest on the leaderboard. Farmer is still the only bettor without a perfect division, but has 3 of 8 division-winner picks currently right (Jaguars, Bills, Broncos), second-most in the pool.

fun_facts.heading: Close Calls at the Top
fun_facts.body: Two division leads are on tiebreakers. The Steelers had a bye and the Bengals won, so both are 6-2 in the AFC North, with Pittsburgh still first. In the AFC West, the Broncos are 7-2 and the Chiefs are 6-2. Cadegn, Dustin, Dilger, and Farmer all picked Denver to win the West, and Dustin and Cadegn have 9 points riding on the Broncos-Chiefs order. The locks are unchanged at 3 of 8: the Bills first, the Patriots second, and the Cardinals last. The Chargers are 0-8, still the only winless team.

closing_paragraph: Cadegn leads by 11, and the next four are within 9 of each other. The NFC South has all four teams within a game, and the AFC North and AFC West leaders are a single game from flipping, so next week could move a lot. Same time next Tuesday.
